_comment: SCRUM-2148 / SCRUM-2149 grandfather baseline for `npm run lint:copy` (scripts/check-copy-terms.ts). Records ONLY pre-existing copy-term violations that the hardened linter (expanded coverage + new §1.3 terms + raw-enum heuristic, SCRUM-2149) surfaced on the 2026-05-30 audit of main@7af0ad9a. The linter PASSES on these exact entries and FAILS on any NEW violation. This is NOT a license to add new violations — every entry must be retired, not extended. Match key = `file` + `line` + `term` (all normalised; term lower-cased, SCRUM-2149 fix2) — a DIFFERENT banned term/raw-enum on an already-baselined line is a NEW violation that fails CI, so `term` is required and load-bearing on every entry. See scripts/agents.md → 'Copy-term grandfather baseline'.
_protocol: ADD an entry only for a genuinely pre-existing violation that cannot be fixed at source in this PR (locked file, or a fix that belongs to another in-flight track).
REMOVE an entry the moment the underlying violation is fixed — a stale entry (file:line no longer violating) is reported as a non-fatal warning by the linter to prompt cleanup.
NEVER add an entry to silence a NEW violation you are introducing — fix it at source or route the value through a display mapper in src/lib/copy.ts.
Line numbers drift when a file is edited above a baselined line; that intentionally turns the entry into a 'new' violation and forces a fix-or-rebaseline decision.

The `term` is part of the match key (SCRUM-2149 fix2): a DIFFERENT banned term/raw-enum field appearing on an already-baselined line is a NEW violation (the recorded entry goes stale). Re-baseline ONLY if the new term is itself genuinely pre-existing and unfixable here — never to absorb a term you are introducing.
